data.title: Cardano expands in Japan – So why is ADA’s price down 4%?
data.description:
Is Cardano [ADA] an integral part of the big player story now? The answer is yes.

The Cardano Foundation recently announced Pacific Meta as an Enterprise Integration Partner in Japan, with the goal of helping Japanese companies figure out where Cardano can actually solve business problems and build solutions.

Under the arrangement, the two organizations will share responsibilities. The Foundation handles the infra and technical support. Pacific Meta takes care of the local side: understanding how Japanese enterprises operate, helping with go-to-market, and doing the hands-on systems integration.

AMBCrypto previously reported that Cardano founder Charles Hoskinson expects Midnight [NIGHT] (the privacy-focused network), to become bigger than Zcash [ZEC].

ADA crypto price drops 4% as shorts take over

Has any of this done much for ADA’s price?

Cardano fell to $0.239 in a single hourly candle on the 2nd of October. That’s a reset of most of the day’s gains. Earlier, ADA tested at $0.26 before sellers pushed it back.

At press time, the RSI fell to 30.55, teetering at the edge of being oversold and well below its signal line at 51.59. The Chaikin Money Flow (CMF) also dropped to -0.10; more capital is flowing out of ADA than coming in.

Open Interest fell to about $258.6 million after the drop; some traders closed their positions. Meanwhile, Funding Rate was at -0.0103, so short sellers are now paying to hold their bets against ADA.

A short-term bounce isn’t off the table. But for now, bears have the upper hand.

Final Summary

  • Cardano Foundation partners with Pacific Meta.
  • ADA price drops; funding is negative and shorts took control.

data.title: ‘Privacy working as intended’: Zano details 1-month rollback after $250M exploit
data.description:
The Zano exploit led to over $250 million in fake assets being minted by the attacker. According to a post-mortem report by the project team, the attacker minted 36.89 million ZANO tokens and $18.45 million fUSD, the Freedom Dollar stablecoin. 

During late August and September, the period when the hack happened and the team noticed the exploit, ZANO’s price averaged between $6.50 and $7.50. Assuming an average price of $7.00, the 38.6 million ZANO tokens and $18.4 million fUSD translated to a total of about $250 million in fake assets. 

Earlier in their preliminary investigation, the Freedom Dollar team said that the attacker exchanged “several million dollars” worth of assets for counterfeit fUSD. This has now been verified, as $18.4 million was swapped for fake minted fUSD. 

Before the hack, fUSD, an algorithmic stablecoin on the privacy-focused Zano network, had a market supply of $12 million, or 12 million fUSD tokens. With the hacker minting 18.45 million fUSD, the supply increased by 153%, or 2.5x higher than the base circulation. 

Similarly, about 15.44 million ZANO were in circulation before the breach. After the 36.89 million fake ZANO tokens were minted, the supply was inflated by 240%.

To address the inflation issue, the team opted to roll back the network by a month. 

Zano hack: The mishap, exploit, and recovery

First, the Zano network is privacy-focused, similar to Zcash. 

To scale adoption and plug in more exchanges and platforms, it had to allow external venues to track the amounts being transferred and spent. That’s what the Gateway Address feature in Hard Fork 6 was supposed to solve. The upgrade went live in late August. 

But there was a code error that led to missing verification for Zano transactions. This allowed the attacker to “hide” extra tokens and mix them with the rest of the legit supply. 

The private nature of the transfers made it challenging to trace these fake asset transfers, making the rollback a logical solution, according to the team. While a drawback, the team hailed it as a plus. 

The major limitation was the traceability of the exploited ZANO and fUSD coins. Once created, they were indistinguishable from any other private ZANO output. That is privacy working as intended. No one, including the Zano team, can accurately determine which outputs are affected.

The rollback has erased the $250 million exploit, with the team assuring the network recovery is stable and ongoing. They plan to explore the Gateway Address again later to facilitate broader integration with exchanges. 

But the ZANO token price was still trading close to $5, a key H2 support level, underscoring that investors were still uncertain about the token after the incident. 

Final Summary

  • Zano team confirmed that nearly $250 million worth of fake ZANO and fUSD was minted by the hacker,
  • The network recovery is stable and ongoing, but investor confidence was still low, per the muted ZANO price,

data.title: Bitcoin clears $85K, but is ‘Uptober’ setting up a bull trap?
data.description:
The “Uptober” frenzy is taking off across the market.

From a technical point of view, BTC’s 42% Q3 rally is already positioning for a better Q4. For BTC, Q4 has historically been one of its strongest quarters, with an average quarterly ROI in excess of 70%. However, for history to repeat itself, October will be crucial in setting the tone for BTC’s Q4 momentum.

This is where the chart below becomes important. According to Glassnode, the sell wall above BTC has largely disappeared. Buyers took out the $85K wall yesterday after nearly a week of failed attempts. So, with less near-term liquidity sitting above BTC, the road higher could also be relatively easy, allowing for the price to move faster if buying takes off.

Notably, the macro setup could also support this move.

As per FedWatch data, rate hike odds dropped from 70% to 26% as expectations of a pause increased. This implies that the market may be slowly starting to price a more liquidity-friendly setup. Up until the recent macro releases, the market was cautious on Bitcoin, with macro FUD acting a key hurdle. Now, with that pressure easing, improving liquidity expectations could give Bitcoin room to extend its momentum.

Interestingly, the momentum seems to be picking up already too. According to CoinGlass, Bitcoin’s long/short ratio was once again above 1. This hinted at an increase in long positioning by traders. So, with the macro FUD easing, liquidity expectations increasing, and the sell wall thinning out, is Bitcoin [BTC] finally gearing up for its “Uptober” momentum?

Is Bitcoin’s $85K breakout a bull trap?

Bitcoin’s ongoing chop could be either accumulation or another fakeout.

While liquidity expectations are improving, the improvement has not been reflected in strong spot buying. U.S Spot Bitcoin ETFs closed September in the red, ending a nine-day inflow streak with $3.1 billion. The funds recorded $148.7 million in net outflows on Wednesday, with Fidelity’s FBTC leading the exits with $125.6 million, while BlackRock’s IBIT saw $9.5 million in outflows, ending its own nine-day inflow streak.

Now, the key question is whether this is the start of sustained outflows. While it’s still too early to confirm a trend, further outflows in this area may put further pressure on Bitcoin. $136.72 million in BTC spot sell orders are stacked between $89K-$109K on Coinbase. This overhead supply could act as resistance if spot buying remains weak, making it harder for Bitcoin to sustain its breakout.

Additionally, the outflows occurred just as rate cut expectations were cooling down, pointing to institutions still not fully pricing in an easier liquidity environment. This, in contrast to the bullish positioning in the Futures market, carving a discrepancy between the spot demand and the derivatives sentiment.

If this situation persists, Bitcoin’s $85K breakout will struggle to sustain itself.

With ETF flows turning red and sell orders building up above, the breakout still needs stronger spot demand to confirm the move. Otherwise, the recent move above $85K can turn into a fakeout, catching late bulls off guard and undermining Bitcoin’s early “Uptober” momentum.

Final Summary

  • Low selling and improving liquidity could push Bitcoin higher.
  • Weak ETF flows and heavy sell orders could turn the $85K breakout into a fakeout.

data.title: Can AAVE crypto reach $200? THIS overbought signal raises concerns
data.description:
Aave [AAVE] might be closing in on a solid profit-taking setup.

From a technical standpoint, the altcoin is up over 20% this week, and is among the top performers in the weekly ranking. The price of AAVE crypto climbed back to where it was at the beginning of January as it rose above $180 to bring both long- and short-term players closer to breakeven. With technicals now overbought, the push towards $200 could see more profit-taking pressure if momentum begins to slow down.

Moreover, with AAVE/BTC up 10%+ this month, it has gained ground for the fourth consecutive week, which suggests that AAVE’s 60%+ rally is not just on the back of the broader market, but also due to strength relative to Bitcoin [BTC]. So, with AAVE/BTC extended, any loss of momentum could increase the risk of a pullback.

In essence, AAVE’s move toward $200 doesn’t look like a straight-line rally.

The main question is what is fueling AAVE crypto’s upside. As mentioned above, more than 60% of its monthly gains are coming from rotational flows, meaning that capital moving from BTC to AAVE appears to be a critical factor. 

So, if BTC.D breaks out and capital starts flowing back to BTC, could that put pressure on AAVE crypto? From a technical perspective, a change in flows could reduce AAVE/BTC momentum and make the path to $200 more challenging, especially with the altcoin already looking stretched.

AAVE crypto’s on-chain momentum puts fuel to the rally

AAVE’s on-chain setup could be giving a different perspective.

In a post on X, the company announced that Aave saw $1.1 trillion in borrow volume. Thus, the demand for lending services on the platform appears to be robust, while its technicals appear to be stretched.

What can support this view is the chart below. According to DeFiLlama data, AAVE crypto closed last month with on-chain figures returning to where they were seen in early June. TVL peaked at almost $20 million, up 18% from the previous month, while fees crossed $37 million, climbing 15% from the same period last year.

Taken together, these figures confirm that Aave’s on-chain activity is growing. The increased TVL speaks of inflows of capital into the platform, and the increasing fees demonstrate the strong lending demand. In other words, the rise in AAVE’s price is justified by its actual usage on-chain.

That makes AAVE’s current upside more than just rotational flows from Bitcoin.

With strong network demand, steady capital flows, and positive technical momentum, AAVE could continue to outperform Bitcoin in the near term, keeping the $200 target in focus.

Final Summary

  • AAVE’s strong rally could push it toward $200, but overbought conditions may trigger profit-taking.
  • Rising TVL, fees, and lending demand show that AAVE’s on-chain activity is also growing.

data.title: Can President Trump’s crypto dinner spark a breakout on the memecoin’s charts?
data.description:
The infamous President Donald Trump crypto dinners are back. The next one, dubbed the Gala Dinner, will be held on 22nd November. It will be the third crypto dinner and will be held at the Trump National Golf Club in Washington. 

The crypto holders, especially his “fans,” who are the top 185 holders of his Official Trump [TRUMP] memecoin, will be granted first access. President Trump had previously stated that he would be at the event. 

Two other events will be extended to TRUMP holders, but the President won’t attend them. One of the events, the F1 Singapore Grand Prix, is reserved only for the top 23 TRUMP holders between 18th July and 5th October. 

The final event will be Super Bowl LXI, but the details are yet to be publicized. These events are run by Fight Fight Fight LLC, a firm registered in Delaware and it is jointly controlled by Trump’s CIC Digital LLC and Celebration Cards. 

For the Gala Dinner, the event promises,

The most exclusive dinner in the world. An evening with 3 legends and President Donald Trump, plus a private meet and greet with a legend to be announced.

The VIP list will be the top 29, with the top 4 TRUMP holders expected to receive 18-karat Trump-branded gold watches. 

Will Trump crypto dinners boost the memecoin?

It’s not clear how much the top 185 holders will spend to get into the event. However, the event will likely spark another backlash from Democrats. 

Notably, similar Trump crypto dinners in April and May 2025 faced massive opposition, with Democrats slamming them as an “orgy of corruption.”

According to Public Citizen, a public watchdog, Trump’s crypto ventures made $1.4B in profits in 2025. Over half of the windfall, $635M, was generated by the TRUMP memecoin. 

On the contrary, Trump crypto investors made a massive $4.7B loss, mainly driven by TRUMP ($3.2B) and World Liberty Financial’s WLFI token ($1B). Put differently, as Trump pocketed a +$600M profit in the TRUMP memecoin, holders lost 5x more than his gains. 

These crypto dealings have forced Democrats to withhold support for the CLARITY Act, a crucial crypto bill. They are now calling for a strict ethics provision to address the alleged corruption by the Trump family.

Worth noting though that TRUMP’s value tripled in Q3 2026, jumping from $1.4 to $3.6. However, it also erased some gains, dipping by 42% to $2.1. It has been consolidating between $1.8 and $2.2 since. As it stands, it’s unclear whether the Gala Dinner will help it break above the range. 

Final Summary

  • Trump will hold another Gala Dinner with the top 185 holders of his memecoin in November.
  • The TRUMP memecoin is stuck within the $1.8-$2.2 price range ahead of the dinner.

data.title: Fidelity exec’s new 60/20/20 portfolio makes room for crypto – Here’s why
data.description:
Should Bitcoin [BTC] have a place in your portfolio? Some investors say it helps spread out risk. Others think it just adds more of it.

The 60/40 portfolio is now 60/20/20

The latest take on this comes from Jurrien Timmer, Global Macro Director at Fidelity.

In a post on X, he said the old 60/40 portfolio, 60% stocks and 40% bonds, has had its day. What’s replaced it is a 60/20/20 split: 60% equities, 20% bonds, and 20% alternative assets.

Timmer says this change kicked in after the pandemic, and he doesn’t see a reason to switch things up right now. The 60/40 setup has been the default for decades, so setting aside a fifth of a portfolio for alternatives is no small thing.

Eventually, Bitcoin will come up in the conversation.

Where BTC fits in this new plan

In Timmer’s updated model, 20% goes to alternative assets. That covers gold, commodities, cash, Bitcoin, REITs, and managed futures.

So why talk about BTC?

BTC’s correlation with the S&P 500 is at 30%, and it has no correlation with US Treasury bonds. Bitcoin doesn’t always move in step with stocks and bonds; exactly what you want from something meant to diversify.

That said, Timmer was clear that this isn’t an optimized portfolio. He called it a rough example of how assets could be split and said it shouldn’t be taken as investment advice.

Notably, this isn’t the first time he’s been upbeat on Bitcoin, either. In an earlier analysis, with the power law model, he predicted a BTC price of $300K by 2029.

AMBCrypto previously reported that Timmer spotted BTC forming a double bottom on the weekly charts. A weekly close above $82K would complete the pattern and clear the way to $100K, a potential 24% upside.

That $82K level mattered on-chain too, since it was also the average cost basis of US spot BTC ETFs.

Final Summary

  • Fidelity’s Jurrien Timmer says the 60/40 portfolio is now 60/20/20; Bitcoin is in the 20% alternatives bucket.
  • BTC’s minimal correlation with Treasuries makes it a diversifier.

data.title: Bitcoin ETFs record $102M inflows – Why $85K matters for BTC now
data.description:
Several Bitcoin [BTC] ETF funds began October with outflows. According to Onchain Lens, five funds recorded a combined $24 million in outflows on the 1st of October. However, strong inflows into three other funds more than made up for these losses. 

BTC ETFs’ net inflow hit $102M amid mixed sentiment

In September, Bitcoin spot ETFs experienced massive inflows. In fact, AMBCrypto reported an accumulation spree with net inflows surpassing $2.5 billion the week ending on the 25th of September. 

This trend has continued into October, with prominent funds recording inflows.

These inflows proved strong enough to turn daily flows positive. BlackRock’s IBIT saw $195 million in inflows, Grayscale’s GBTC recorded $14 million in inflows, and Morgan Stanley’s MSBT recorded $7 million in inflows. 

For that reason, the daily net inflow rose to $102 million, marking a significant reversal from -$148 million recorded in the previous session. 

With ETF inflows remaining resilient despite recent headwinds, investors appear to be aggressively seeking Bitcoin exposure through these funds.

Moreover, a look at past cycles shows that sustained ETF inflows have worked well for BTC price action. 

Exchange activity is also echoing the shift in ETF capital flow. Exchange Netflow has held positive since the 30th of September.

As ETFs resumed accumulating again, supply outflows from exchanges recovered. Spot Netflow fell to -$67 million as of writing, down from $353 million the previous day. 

Any impact on BTC?

On the 2nd of October, Bitcoin made a major upswing as BTC finally managed to flip $85k.

At press time, Bitcoin was trading around $86,272, up 3.3% on the daily charts. The recent upsurge could be attributed to renewed demand, especially driven by ETF and Uptober speculation. 

For now, the market leans bullish based on the directional indicators. However, the momentum is relatively weak. 

For example, Aroon Up was hovering around 21%, having declined for eleven consecutive days. Moreover, if the capital inflow holds steady as recently witnessed, the trend will continue, with Bitcoin reclaiming $88k and eyeing $90k. 

However, if the latest attempt fails to produce a daily close above $85k, the crypto is likely to revisit $82k.

Final summary

  • Bitcoin climbed 3% to a weekly high of $86,912, then retraced to $86,272 at press time. 
  • BTC Spot ETFs recorded $102 million in daily Net Inflows, a reversal from -$148 million recorded the previous session.

data.title: XLM price prediction – Why Stellar’s $0.21 rebound could trigger a 9% rally
data.description:
Stellar’s XLM, like the rest of the altcoin market, gave back part of its recent gains. It fell about 9% from the Q3 high of $0.23 to a low of $0.21. However, it tagged a short-term support level that has seen a spike in demand and could reverse the recent decline and offer a 9% gain. 

XLM price extends uptrend momentum

On the price charts, the altcoin was already up 4% after defending the range low of the rising channel (blue). 

In the past two weeks, XLM has been making higher lows and higher highs, printing the rising channel pattern. Simply put, the altcoin uptrend momentum has been steadily rising.  

For traders, the channel’s range lows and highs have offered trading opportunities since mid-September. If the trend extends, XLM could target the range high ($0.25). That would translate to a 14% potential upside if hit. 

But it must first clear the recent price high of $0.23 and the mid-channel range. If the immediate hurdle is hit, that would be a 9% gain from the $0.21 support. 

At press time, the Relative Strength Index (RSI) was above the neutral line, further suggesting there was more room for an upside move. 

The short-term bullish outlook would be invalidated in case of a bearish breakout below the rising channel. Such a move would open a downside risk scenario to $0.20. 

Whale activity could fuel XLM price recovery

That said, the liquidation heatmap showed an upside pool right below $0.24, which aligned with the mid-channel range and $0.23 level mentioned above. 

As such, in case of volatility-driven market swings, the target could be reached, further reinforcing the bullish thesis and 9% potential gain. 

Besides, CryptoQuant indicated a spike in whale buying during the recent pullback. The renewed whale interest could help the altcoin defend the range lows and boost the uptrend. 

Overall, the fact that the recent 4% rebound was also being driven by spot bidding by whales could bolster bulls’ push to $0.23 or higher. But a breach below the short-term rising channel would be a warning sign of building selling pressure, effectively invalidating the bullish thesis. 

Final Summary

  • Stellar’s XLM defended its short-term support above $0.21 amid whale spot bids 
  • The recovery gain could extend to 9-14% if XLM maintains its short-term trend

data.title: Quant price prediction — What next after profit taking causes QNT to drop by 18%?
data.description:
Is the hype around QNT fading? After facing rejection at $326, Quant lost the $300-support and fell to a low of $237.

At press time, QNT was trading at around $239, down 18% on the daily charts. Over the same window, the spot trading volume fell by 33% to $474 million too. 

This fall in value was driven largely by intense selling pressure as investors turned to cash out their recent gains. Just recently, the altcoin recorded 250% weekly gains, with the same leading to significant profit-taking. This market behavior has now possibly become even more stubborn. 

Quant investors reduce exposure after a parabolic rally

As Quant’s [QNT] decline persisted on the charts, a significant share of bulls were kicked out of the market. According to Coinglass, QNT saw over $4.8 million in total liquidations. Longs suffered the most, with $3.5 million in longs liquidated.

The elevated liquidation risk, especially for longs, triggered fear. As a result, traders hurriedly closed their positions. 

Within a single 24-hour period, Quant Futures recorded $480 million in outflows compared to $453 million in inflows. As a result, the Futures Netflow fell by 1120% to -$26.7 million. 

Such a massive drop in Netflow hinted at risk aversion, with traders choosing to exit before the price dropped further. 

On top of that, the altcoin’s Open Interest seemed to confirm this shift in sentiment as it fell by 15% to $167 million. 

A look at the Spot market

The Spot market saw elevated profit-taking throughout the recent price hike. A look at the Spot Netflows revealed that the metric has mostly been positive since the rally started.

Over the past week, Netflows fell negative only twice. At press time, the metric sat around $1.3 million, marking a notable reversal from -$11 million the previous day.

Such a shift in flow suggests that most investors are actively cashing out. High profit realization creates more downside pressure on the charts.

In fact, every time the Netflow climbed into the positive zone, the price retraced. The trend is likely to continue this time too.

Can QNT hold the pressure?

On the daily charts, QNT’s upside momentum seemed to have weakened considerably. A look at the Normalized RVGI revealed that this momentum indicator has declined for three consecutive days, falling to 30 at press time.

A falling NRVGI alludes to fading bullish momentum. Likewise, the Relative Strength Index (RSI) has also continued to drop, forming a bearish crossover.

The RSI was still holding at around 69 though, suggesting that buyers are yet to fully lose control. However, if profit-taking continues, Quant will likely see more losses.

Further losses at the press time price level will lead to a drop below $200, with $195 as a critical support level. If market bulls hold on, reclaiming $300 will remain on the table though.

Final summary

  • Quant [QNT] fell by 18%, lost its $300-support and dropped to a low of $236. 
  • Altcoin is facing selling pressure across the market thanks to risk-off sentiment.

data.title: RENDER crypto tests $2 again – Could bulls finally break through?
data.description:
Render crypto has entered October at a key inflection point.

Technically, the AI-related token jumped over 35% in September, pushing back toward the $2 level. However, this is a critical resistance for RENDER, as the altcoin has failed to break this barrier three times since the October crash. Therefore, RENDER is at another inflection point ahead of Q4.

Obviously, the main question is whether this is a fourth rejection or a breakout attempt. Given that the bullish trend in the AI space is gaining ground, the overall environment will be a critical factor in determining the direction of RENDER.

As the chart above shows, the combined market cap of AI coins closed September with a 47%+ rally.

To put this into perspective, more than $12 billion in capital inflows took the sector’s market cap back toward mid-Q4 2025 levels, when it crossed $35 billion. In fact, September marked the strongest monthly rally, while Q3 saw the strongest quarterly rally, with the total AI-coin market cap climbing 61%.

In essence, the AI sector is off to a roaring start in Q4, providing Render [RENDER] with the much-needed boost as it tests the $2 resistance zone once again. However, the intriguing development is that this momentum is now beginning to translate on-chain too, adding another layer to the overall bullish setup.

RENDER bulls face the $2 barrier

RENDER’s September growth was obviously influenced by the continued rise of AI.

While RENDER had a relatively weak start to Q3, it has grown more than 61% in the current quarter, with more than half of the volume concentrated in the last month. Most importantly, this growth also saw a significant increase in the on-chain volume of the Render Network.

As can be seen in the chart below, RENDER crossed more than $1.85 billion in trading volume, far surpassing the figures of the previous months. Thus, it appears that trading volume has begun to accelerate, its highest level of the quarter.

And so, RENDER’s on-chain volume has resumed its growth in line with the overall rise of the AI narrative.

However, the price of $2 is the critical level to watch. 

A break above this resistance with increased trading volume on the third attempt would be a significant development for RENDER. With growing optimism around AI and the rise in on-chain activity, bulls have more reason to be optimistic about the altcoin’s prospects in the near future.

If RENDER manages to hold above $2, the recent recovery could gain further traction.

Final Summary
